llm.summary: This skill performs straightforward PDF splitting and PDF-to-Word conversion, with ordinary file read/write behavior and no hidden network, credential, persistence, or privilege behavior found.

dimensions.detail: Filesystem access to read PDFs and write derived PDF/DOCX files is proportionate to the purpose, but users should ensure paths point only to intended workspace files.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses npm dependencies for PDF and DOCX handling. The package has a lockfile, but package.json uses caret ranges, the lockfile resolves through npmmirror, and the supplied scan flags nanoid 5.1.7 as vulnerable.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions ask the agent to map user requests into absolute input and output paths; output-file creation is disclosed, but overwrite behavior and workspace containment are not explicitly defined.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No evidence of persistence, background workers, credential/session access, privilege escalation, tool hijacking, memory writes, destructive deletion, or runtime network exfiltration was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose matches the implementation: it reads a user-specified PDF, either copies selected pages into a new PDF or extracts text into a DOCX, and returns a simple success message.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with an npm-based local document tool. Use explicit output paths in a workspace directory, avoid overwriting important files, and consider updating or pinning dependencies before use because the supplied scan reports a vulnerable transitive nanoid version.
llm.findings:
[SC4] expected: The affected nanoid package is a transitive dependency through docx, which is purpose-aligned for DOCX creation; this is a real dependency-maintenance issue, not evidence of malicious skill behavior.
[SQP-2] expected: Writing output PDF and DOCX files is central to the skill and is described via outputPath fields; the skill would be clearer if it documented overwrite handling and path constraints.
[SQP-3] expected: The Chinese install wording is consistent with the bilingual examples and does not create a security concern.
[SC1] expected: The pdf-lib, pdf-parse, and docx dependencies are aligned with the skill purpose; caret ranges reduce reproducibility despite the committed lockfile, so dependency pinning would improve supply-chain hygiene.
